title: Normalized slice tensor comparison preserves coefficient scalar action
statement: For a small ringed site and its slice [def-weil-size-convention, def-pur-localized-ringed-site], fix derived closed structures, K-flat tensor comparisons and full tensor coherences [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal, def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model]. Given normalized slice tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-evaluation-transpose], the coefficient identification furnished by termwise restriction and localization makes scalar action commute with restriction on every derived object. Explicitly, restriction of tensoring with the inverse coefficient-unit identification and then the right unitor equals tensor comparison, the restricted coefficient identification, inverse slice coefficient-unit identification, and slice right unitor.

proof.text: The termwise restriction functor identifies the single coefficient complex with the single coefficient complex on the slice. Compose this single-complex isomorphism with the fixed localization isomorphism to construct the coefficient identification. The coefficient complex is flat-term and K-flat by its single-term boundedness and tensor-unit flatness. Flatness of the nonzero coefficient term follows directly from its tensor-unit isomorphism, without choosing a closed structure.

On a flat-term K-flat representative compare source and slice scalar-action models with the tensor restriction model. After canceling the tensor comparison the two maps agree: in coefficient degree zero both send x tensor a to a times x, and in other coefficient degrees the source summand is zero. Sheafification and coproduct universal properties detect this equality.

Localize the chain identity, use localization and model-comparison naturality, and cancel the model isomorphisms to obtain scalar compatibility on representatives. Resolve an arbitrary derived object by a flat-term K-flat complex and transport the equation by tensor-comparison and right-unitor naturality. The site tensor-right comparison transports flatness between the abstract tensor-right functor and IsFlatOnSite.

theorem ringedSlice_scalar_unit :
    let r := ringedSliceDerivedRestriction.{c, v, r, w, w'} J R U
    let O := DerivedCategory.Q.obj (ringedTensorUnitComplex.{c, v, r} J R)
    let OU := DerivedCategory.Q.obj
      (ringedTensorUnitComplex.{max c v, v, r} (J.over U) (R.over U))
    ∃ o : r.obj O ≅ OU, ∀ N,
      r.map (S.tensor.map (X := (N, O)) (Y := (N, S.monoidal.tensorUnit))
        (𝟙 N, K.unitIso.inv) ≫ (S.monoidal.rightUnitor N).hom) =
        (d.rho N O).hom ≫ SU.tensor.map
          (X := (r.obj N, r.obj O)) (Y := (r.obj N, OU)) (𝟙 (r.obj N), o.hom) ≫
          SU.tensor.map (X := (r.obj N, OU))
            (Y := (r.obj N, SU.monoidal.tensorUnit)) (𝟙 (r.obj N), KU.unitIso.inv) ≫
              (SU.monoidal.rightUnitor (r.obj N)).hom
